title: Of Offences by or Relating to Public Servants
shortDescription: Offences by public servants who misuse their position — disobeying the law to cause injury, failing to register FIRs in serious offences, falsifying records, trading or buying property against legal bars — plus hospitals refusing to treat victims, and people who impersonate public servants or wear their uniform.
summary:
Chapter XII deals with the misuse of public office and with people who pretend to hold it. It corresponds to Chapter IX of the IPC, which ran from s.166 to s.171. The IPC's bribery offences (ss.161-165A) had already been repealed in 1988 and moved to the Prevention of Corruption Act, so they do not appear here. The BNS keeps the remaining eight sections in the same order, and each BNS section maps to one IPC section: 198 to 166, 199 to 166A, 200 to 166B, 201 to 167, 202 to 168, 203 to 169, 204 to 170 and 205 to 171. The Gazette gives the chapter no sub-headings; the sections fall into three groups: public servants breaking legal duties (ss.198-201), unlawful trade and purchases (ss.202-203), and impersonating public servants (ss.204-205).

Section 198 punishes a public servant who knowingly disobeys a direction of law about how he must do his job, intending or knowing it likely to cause injury to a person (simple imprisonment up to one year). Section 199 is aimed at investigating officers: knowingly breaking the rules that forbid summoning certain persons for investigation, or other rules on how an investigation is conducted, or — most importantly — failing to record an FIR under BNSS s.173(1) for rape and related sexual offences, acid attack and trafficking. It carries a mandatory minimum of six months' rigorous imprisonment, up to two years, and fine. Section 200 makes the person in charge of any hospital, government or private, liable for up to one year if it fails to give the immediate free treatment to rape and acid-attack victims required by BNSS s.397. Section 201 punishes a public servant who knowingly prepares or translates an official document or electronic record incorrectly to cause injury (up to three years).

Sections 202 and 203 prevent conflicts of interest. A public servant legally barred from trade who engages in trade faces simple imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both — and the BNS now adds community service as an option. A public servant legally barred from buying certain property who buys or bids for it, even through another person, faces simple imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both, and the property is confiscated.

Section 204 punishes pretending to hold a public office, or personating a real office-holder, and acting under colour of that office. The BNS makes it far more serious than s.170 IPC: at least six months, up to three years, and a compulsory fine; it is cognizable and non-bailable. Section 205 punishes wearing a public servant's garb or carrying a token resembling theirs so that people believe one belongs to that class; its fine rises from ₹200 to ₹5,000. Sections 199, 201, 204 and 205 are cognizable; the rest are non-cognizable. All are bailable except s.204, and none is compoundable.

  - RI 6 months - 2 yrs + fine
- Hospital not treating victim (s.200)
  - BNSS s.397; public or private
- Incorrect document (s.201)
  - 3 yrs
## Trade & property (ss.202-203)
- Unlawful trade (s.202)
  - Community service — NEW
- Buying barred property (s.203)
  - Confiscation
## Impersonation (ss.204-205)
- Personating public servant (s.204)
  - 6 months - 3 yrs + fine; non-bailable
- Garb or token (s.205)
  - 3 months / ₹5,000
